native_decisions.rationale: The instruction requests picking up the mint green scissors and lifting them by 10 cm. Current RGB shows the scissors near the right arm, and the instruction-grounded-pickup operation matches the manipulation objective with instruction-grounded object localization, appearance-conditioned grasp, and reachable lifting. Its observation-batch input and action-chunk output match the episode contracts, so no other structured operation is needed.

The instruction is a single-object grasp-and-lift task: locate the mint green scissors, grasp them, and lift by 10 cm. Current RGB shows scissors on the tabletop with pale mint-green handles, so the scene has the required target object. Among the structured operations, instruction-grounded-pickup explicitly provides instruction grounding, appearance-conditioned grasp, and reachable lifting, matching the requested manipulation. Other structured operations target placement, insertion, pouring/transfer, button pressing, or tool-mediated alignment rather than pickup. A learned composition could produce actions, but the structured pickup capability has explicit compatible support for this manipulation objective.

The scissors are visible, so the structured capability fits better than an unspecialized learned composition.

The structured operation library contains a compatible capability: footprint-relative-placement explicitly covers visual shape grounding and footprint-relative placement with grasp-and-place control, matching the instruction to put each visible tool into its corresponding shaped position in the toolbox. Its observation-batch input and action-chunk output contracts match the episode, and the nonempty instruction plus 480x640x3 head RGB condition are satisfied. Missing structured tool/toolbox labels are not a mismatch; the current RGB and instruction provide the object roles. The final arm reset is a shared lifecycle action and does not disqualify this manipulation operation.

native_decisions.rationale: The prior bind failed at inference with zero executed actions, and the current observation shows RGB available on all three cameras with both end-effector joint states at 1.0, satisfying the slot-insertion restart preconditions. Because no physical motion occurred, the scene is unchanged, and slot-insertion remains the capability whose declared contract (object-slot geometry grounding, reachable assignment, alignment refresh, insertion, release) matches the instruction to place each tool into its matching toolbox position; the arm reset is shared lifecycle behavior. Restart discards the stale skill state and recomputes the same capability from the current RGB and proprioception rather than switching capabilities or aborting.
